Filegate' May Be Good for Us
nytimes_articles.abstract:
Filegate" may have a silver lining. Civil libertarians have long been concerned about the Government's extensive files on American citizens, but have  been thwarted, mostly by Republican judges and politicians, in their attempts to rein in the Federal Government. Now that Republicans are outraged that the Clinton Administration obtained F.B.I. files on more than 300 prominent Republicans, maybe the average American citizen can finally get some protection. 

     Years ago, as a lawyer for the American Civil Liberties Union, I brought the  first two lawsuits challenging the practice of building dossiers on antiwar and  civil rights advocates. At the time, it was taken for granted that the F.B.I. and many state and local law enforcement agencies kept extensive files on such lawful activities as attending meetings, petitioning, demonstrating and distributing leaflets.

For casual fans of sports like gymnastics, basketball and track, the Olympics on network television are considered a good break from summer reruns.      During Monday night workouts in the pool at John Jay College of Criminal Justice, the runners wear flotation belts while they jog, walk, sprint or hurdle in place for 45 minutes. It is hard work but easy on the joints.
